name: BulkPublish
tagline: Queue a spreadsheet of posts once and let it publish across every connected social account

pricing.notes: Pro listed at $13.99/month monthly and $11.89/month billed annually ($142.70/yr); Business $39.99/month. Priced per organization, not per seat. X publishing is metered separately in credits on every plan.
pricing.freeTier: The free plan covers three channels, thirty posts a month, ten scheduled at a time and 100 MB of media, with repeat posts and RSS auto-publishing held back for paid plans.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 3 channels (1/platform); 3 posts/day and 30/month; 10 scheduled posts; 100 MB media; 30 API requests/day; 1 organization; 50 AI captions/month plus credits; 1 RSS draft feed; no repeat posts.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 2 channels/platform; 30 posts/day (900/month); 30 scheduled/day; 2 GB media; 5 API keys; 5,000 API requests/day; 3 organizations; 10 repeat posts; 300 AI captions/month; 10 RSS auto-publish feeds.
tiers.notes: Annual equivalent reflects the advertised 15% discount.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 5 channels/platform; unlimited posts; 100 scheduled/day; 10 GB media; 10 API keys; 50,000 API requests/day; 10 organizations; unlimited repeats; 1,000 AI captions/month; 50 RSS auto-publish feeds.
tiers.notes: Annual equivalent reflects the advertised 15% discount.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 3 channels (1/platform); 3 posts/day and 30/month; 10 scheduled posts; 100 MB media; 30 API requests/day; 1 organization; 50 AI captions/month plus credits; 1 RSS draft feed; no repeat posts
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (15% lower on annual billing)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Publishing to X uses separate pay-as-you-go credits, and additional AI credits can add cost; current public unit prices were not exposed.

verdictSummary: The part people picture is a weekend: a list of posts, a timer, one API call each. The part that eats the next six months is everything after the first successful post · staying authenticated to a dozen networks, learning each one's media rules the hard way, publishing that reports success and then quietly fails minutes later, retries that must never post twice, and a review process before some networks will accept a post at all. Build it for two accounts you control and it works. Build it for every network on the marketing page and you have taken a job.
coreLoopDIY: Import a spreadsheet of captions and images, point each row at one or more connected accounts, and let it publish on schedule with a log of what landed.
requirements: a developer app and API credentials per network (several need review before they will publish anything)
somewhere always on for the schedule to fire
somewhere to keep the posts and the media
patience for the retry and duplicate-post edge cases
whatYouLose: staying connected · networks expire your auth and someone has to notice
knowing a post is malformed before the network rejects it, not after
an honest publish status when a network accepts the upload and fails minutes later
approvals, teams and multiple client workspaces
the platform review process that gates posting on some networks entirely
moatNotes: The moat is not the scheduler, it is the standing cost of a dozen platform integrations that change under you.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a scheduler is only worth anything when it is boring, and a self-built one stops being boring the first time a token expires overnight or a network changes its video rules without telling anyone. People pay so that maintenance is somebody else's Tuesday.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Open-source multi-network scheduler · the most complete working example to read before starting.

priorArt.name: Mixpost
priorArt.desc: Self-hosted scheduler with a smaller, more readable codebase than the alternatives.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: The broadest open scheduler here; free means running PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal and your own platform credentials.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose for self-hosting.
facts.engines: Optional AI/media features connect to OpenAI, ElevenLabs, fal.ai, Tavily, KieAI and Transloadit.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL holds application data; Redis and Temporal support jobs; media is stored locally or in Cloudflare R2/S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Postiz is not a spreadsheet-first one-upload queue, so large batches require more workflow work as well as operating its server stack.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is straightforward; self-hosting requires Docker, social OAuth apps, and a PostgreSQL, Redis and Temporal stack.

alternatives.name: Mixpost Lite
alternatives.desc: A polished single-user scheduler with queues and basic analytics; the team features live in the paid edition.

facts.install: Docker Compose is recommended; a manual Laravel/Composer installation is also documented.
facts.dataFormat: MySQL stores application data, Redis handles queues/cache, and media uses local/public disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Mixpost Lite is single-user and does not offer BulkPublish's purpose-built spreadsheet-to-many-accounts flow.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server with Docker plus social-platform app credentials; the manual path also needs PHP, Composer, Supervisor, cron, Redis and FFmpeg.

alternatives.name: Publer Free
alternatives.desc: Three non-X accounts and ten queued posts each, with a bulk CSV importer that is the closest free match for the actual job.

facts.install: Hosted signup and OAuth connection to each social account.
facts.dataFormat: Connected-account metadata, scheduled content, media and analytics live in Publer's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: Publer's free CSV importer accepts only five posts per upload, turning a true bulk job into repeated small imports.

alternatives.name: Social Champ Free
alternatives.desc: Three non-X accounts, fifteen queued posts each, analytics and an inbox; one user and no X publishing.

facts.install: Hosted signup and OAuth connection to each social profile.
facts.engines: Champ AI Suite is included, but Social Champ's public documentation does not identify the underlying model provider.
facts.dataFormat: Posts, media, profile metadata, inbox data and analytics live in Social Champ's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan excludes X and caps each of three profiles at fifteen scheduled posts, which sharply limits a bulk queue.

alternatives.name: Buffer Free
alternatives.desc: Three channels, ten queued posts each and thirty days of metrics; eight lifetime channel connections make swapping a one-way door.

facts.install: Hosted signup, with optional desktop browser extension and mobile apps.
facts.engines: Buffer AI Assistant is included, but Buffer's public product documentation does not identify its underlying model provider.
facts.dataFormat: Posts, media, ideas, connected-account metadata and analytics are stored in Buffer's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: Buffer Free lacks a comparable high-volume CSV-first importer and allows only ten queued posts per channel.

alternatives.name: Fedica Free
alternatives.desc: Ten network accounts and ten queued posts total, refilling forever; generous until you plan eleven things at once.

facts.install: Hosted signup and OAuth connection to each social account.
facts.dataFormat: Connected profiles, drafts, scheduled posts, media and analytics live in Fedica's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: Fedica permits only ten scheduled posts at once across the whole free account, so a spreadsheet-sized batch cannot remain queued.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Zapier free plan
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The usual DIY answer for bulk posting from a sheet, but the free tier is single-step Zaps with a monthly task cap · it is a trigger, not a scheduler, and it runs out mid-campaign.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Meta Business Suite Planner
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Genuinely free and genuinely good, but only for Facebook and Instagram · it is not an alternative to posting everywhere at once.

notes: Bulk-first scheduler · the honest split between the one-weekend build and the multi-year integration bill is unusually clean here.
prompt:
Build me a personal bulk social scheduler to replace BulkPublish. Requirements:

- Python 3.12 + FastAPI + SQLite, Jinja templates, no JavaScript framework.
  One process on an always-on box, APScheduler ticking once a minute.
- Two networks only: Mastodon (access token) and Bluesky (app password).
  One small module per network behind a single publish(post, account)
  function so a third is addable later. Scaffold nothing I do not use.
- The main screen is a CSV importer. Columns: caption, image, send_at,
  accounts. Show me every parsed row with a per-network character count and
  a red flag on anything too long or missing a file, and import only the
  rows that pass.
- Rows with no send_at fall into posting times I configure per account
  (weekdays 09:00 and 17:00 in my timezone) and take the next free one.
- Each tick picks up due rows one at a time and flips the row to "sending"
  in its own transaction before any network call, so a crash or a double
  tick can never post the same row twice. Then "sent" with the live post
  URL, or "failed" with the error text. Three retries, backing off, and
  never a retry once a send is confirmed.
- Images copied into media/ beside the database, checked for type and size
  at import, removed 90 days after the row sends.
- A history page: last 200 rows, status, error, link to the live post, and
  a retry button.
- Out of scope, and say so plainly in the README: X, Instagram, LinkedIn
  and TikTok (paid, approval-gated or review-gated APIs), analytics,
  approvals, and more than one user.
- README covers getting a Mastodon token and a Bluesky app password.
  Secrets in .env, localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry.
